# Cipi — Full Site Content for LLMs

> Last updated: 2026-10-23. Canonical site: https://cipi.sh — index of pages: https://cipi.sh/llms.txt

## URL structure

English only. Public URLs have no language prefix: homepage `https://cipi.sh/`, docs `https://cipi.sh/docs/`, and so on. `/en/…` 301s to the same path without `/en`. Former language trees and localized slugs 301 to the English equivalent. There is no Accept-Language or cookie redirect.

URLs below are the public English paths.

## What is Cipi

Cipi is a free, open-source (MIT), Laravel-first deploy CLI for Ubuntu VPS. One command installs a complete production stack — Nginx, PHP 8.x (PHP-FPM or Laravel Octane on FrankenPHP), MariaDB (optional PostgreSQL), Valkey, Supervisor — on any fresh Ubuntu 24.04/26.04 server. It also supports static sites and generic PHP apps. Cipi is CLI-first with a REST API, a remote CLI client, an MCP server for AI agents, and an optional self-hosted web control panel (GUI). It is a self-hosted alternative to Laravel Forge with no subscription and no per-server fee.

- Install: `wget -O - https://cipi.sh/setup.sh | bash` (run on a fresh Ubuntu VPS)
- Admin access: SSH as `cipi` user, then `sudo cipi …` (no password, `cipi` only) or `su root` with the root password from the installation summary — not `sudo -s` (the `cipi` user's password is random and never shown) Since 5.8.2 `sudo cipi credentials` prints the install credentials again (root, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, Valkey, Meilisearch master key, backup key, with connection URLs) and `cipi credentials export` writes them as a plain CSV (`title,url,username,password,notes`) for any password manager; the installer accepts several SSH keys, shows a plan before installing, and waits until the credentials are confirmed saved before offering the panel API and GUI as yes/no questions.
- License: MIT, source at https://github.com/cipi-sh/cipi
- Author: Andrea Pollastri (https://github.com/andreapollastri)
- Current major version: Cipi 5.8.4 (5.8.4: `cipi deploy <app> --status [--json] [--tail=N]` — is a deploy running right now, whoever started it: Git push, CLI, panel, cipi/agent, rollback; state running/queued/interrupted/idle, phase, trigger, elapsed, last result, optional log tail; the panel shows deploys it did not start with their live log (cipi/gui 4.1.0 via cipi/api 1.37.0 `GET /api/apps/{name}/deploy/status`, `deploy-manage`) and opens each audit row's log; a failed post-deploy healthcheck says where the check comes from and how to change or remove it (`cipi health set <app> --url=|--no-postdeploy`, `cipi health unset`), a 404 noting Laravel serves `/up` only with the health route on; `cipi health set --no-postdeploy` keeps the URL/status already set; `cipi yml example` ships `health:` commented out; 5.8.3: security — the panel API shows a job (`GET /api/jobs/{id}`) only to a token holding the ability the job was created under, `404` otherwise, cipi/api 1.36.1; jobs that hold a password are pruned after a day. 5.8.2: the installer accepts several SSH keys (`Add another SSH public key?`; `SSH_PUBKEY` one per line), shows a plan and asks `Proceed? [Y/n]` before the first package, prints the credentials in one layout (title, User:, Password:, Host:, URL:) and waits until `y` to "Have you saved these credentials?", then offers the panel API and the GUI as yes/no questions; `cipi api <domain>` and `cipi gui <domain>` check the DNS first (`--skip-dns-check`), install and issue the certificate (`--no-ssl`), `cipi api` offers the first token (`--no-token`), `cipi api|gui ssl` and `move` run the same check; `cipi credentials` prints the install summary again (root, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, Valkey, Meilisearch master key, backup key, with connection URLs) and `cipi credentials export [--output=FILE]` writes a plain CSV `title,url,username,password,notes`; `cipi gui sso set|status|only on|off|disable` configures single sign-on over OpenID Connect for the panel (cipi/gui 4.0.2); fixes: `cipi gui update` left the panel on the old package (composer path repository, now `composer reinstall`), `cipi yml plan` never reached "in sync". 5.8.1: fix — `cipi deploy` exited 1 after a successful deploy since 5.2.3 (a trailing `[[ … ]] && return` under `set -e`), so cipi/api and every client (GUI, cipi-cli, MCP tools) reported deploys started through the API as failed while the release was live; the post-deploy steps now print as they run and end with `✓ Post-deploy: <summary>`; webhook deploys were not affected; no migration. 5.8.0: environments — `cipi app create --env=<label>` (default `production`; `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}$`), `cipi app edit --env`, `cipi app clone --env`, `cipi app show` prints the environment, written to .env as `APP_ENV` (Laravel) and `CIPI_ENV` (Laravel and Node); an app with env `<label>` reads `cipi-<label>.yml` before `cipi.yml` in `current/`, `htdocs/` and `shared/`, so one repository serves a staging and a production app, the server choosing the file and an invalid `cipi-<label>.yml` having no fallback; new `deploy.branch` in cipi.yml sets the deploy branch like `cipi app edit --branch`, from the next deploy; `cipi yml auto status` prints env and file, `--json` outputs carry `env`, nginx denies `/cipi-<anything>.yml|yaml`; panel API 1.36.0 (MCP server 1.6.0), cipi-cli 1.9.0, PHP SDK 1.4.0, GUI 4.0.0, cipi/agent 2.1.0 and Cipi Studio 2.4.17 carry `env`; migration 5.8.0 adds `CIPI_ENV=production` to existing apps and updates vhosts; 5.7.2: `cipi use <app>` default app, `CIPI_DEPLOY_BRANCH` and `REDIS_*` in a new app's .env, deploy durations in `--releases`, forge errors that say what the token needs, `cipi backup profile remove --purge`; 5.7.1: Octane (FrankenPHP) apps load the FPM pool hardening from `/etc/php/cipi-octane.d` through `PHP_INI_SCAN_DIR` — `session.upload_progress.enabled=0`, the mitigation for CVE-2026-115560 (PHP advisory of 2026-10-23, no fix yet) and for the upload-progress path of CVE-2026-109619; 5.7.0: `cipi api move` and `cipi gui move` change the panel domain in one command — the certificate follows — `cipi api remove` uninstalls the API, and a panel domain can no longer be shared with an app; 5.6.4: cipi.yml auto-apply on Git-webhook deploys, `--json` on `cipi yml plan` and `cipi yml auto status`, cipi.yml from the panel API 1.35; 5.6.3: security release for the PHP advisory of 2026-10-21, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 — `cipi php upgrade` runs daily at 03:30, reports each PHP version and each Octane FrankenPHP binary as patched, VULNERABLE, distro or END OF LIFE and exits 1 while one is vulnerable; every Cipi-written FPM pool turns off `session.upload_progress.enabled` and, on PHP 8.5, `fatal_error_backtraces`; PHP packages come from packages.sury.org first, then the ondrej PPA, and the migration moves existing servers to sury.org; 5.6.2: a failed PostgreSQL restore no longer empties the database — wipe and import in one transaction, empty dumps refused, schema owner fixed; 5.6.1: `deploy.post` `artisan` steps run — they all failed as `/usr/bin/phpX.Yartisan` — and a failed step reports its real exit code, so `post_on_failure: abort` fails the deploy; 5.6.0: `cipi app create` opens with menus — app type, PHP-FPM or Octane, MariaDB or PostgreSQL — and asks for the asset build; `cipi db create` asks the engine the same way; the deploy key is tested against the repository on create, `app edit --repository|--branch` and `cipi git check`, with an offer to save or replace the forge token; named S3 backup destinations (`cipi backup destination add`) so one profile ships to several buckets; fixed: failed PostgreSQL restores reported as done, a cipi.yml cron with a newline, lists losing their columns with long names; no migration. 5.5.2: panel API sudoers allow `cipi disk` and `cipi disk *`, so cipi/api 1.33 can serve disk usage read-only. The same release aligns `cipi.yml` with the server: `deploy.node_build` is the Laravel asset build before the release goes live (`deploy.post` runs after), `deploy.predeploy_snapshot` is the pre-deploy snapshot (`snapshot` still accepted), `cipi yml generate --save` writes `/home/<app>/cipi.yml` (apply still reads the committed copy), backup profiles the file drops leave the schedule (archives stay for `cipi backup prune`), and the deploy-success mail quotes the auto-apply result. 5.5.1: wildcard certificates install and renew end to end — Cipi writes the HTTPS vhost, certbot only issues/renews; DNS-01 certificates are reissued over DNS-01; renewals reload nginx; `cipi ssl status` per app; `cipi app list` runtime fix. 5.5.0: `cipi disk` and `cipi disk db` — disk usage of the server, of every app (files, database, total, % of disk) and of every MariaDB, PostgreSQL, Valkey and Meilisearch database in MB; soft per-app disk limits with `cipi app limits <app> --disk=<GB>|none` and a new `app_disk` monitor check (warn at 90%, crit when over, nothing blocked, not reconcilable from cipi.yml); `cipi firewall attempts` sets fail2ban's SSH threshold (default 3) in a drop-in updates never reset; `cipi ssh apps enable|disable <app>|--all` controls app users' SSH/SFTP from other machines, deploys over ssh localhost unaffected; several named Cloudflare accounts for DNS-01 (`cipi ssl dns set --name=`, `ssl install --account=`, `ssl dns list|remove`); fixed: Laravel logs now use `LOG_CHANNEL=single` and actually follow the 12-month retention, tab-completion works after `sudo cipi` and in non-login shells, the installer names containers instead of misreporting the Ubuntu version; migration 5.5.0 switches Laravel apps to single, folds dated logs into laravel.log and gracefully restarts running workers/Horizon/Octane/Reverb and reloads PHP-FPM where the .env changed. 5.4.1: panel API sudoers open `cipi redirect`, `cipi proxy add|remove|list` and `cipi node list|status|restart` to cipi/api 1.31.0 and the GUI; Node runtime installs, search/package installs and `zt` changes stay CLI-root. 5.4.0: Node apps — `cipi app create --node=spa|static|ssr` with Next.js, Nuxt, SvelteKit, Astro, Remix and Vite presets, SPA fallback to /index.html, static sites with real 404s, SSR with blue/green Supervisor slots that switch only after the health path answers, webhooks without cipi/agent, `cipi node status|restart|logs`; `cipi node install|list|upgrade|remove` for checksum-verified official Node builds and `cipi node default <major>|system` as the server-wide Node for Laravel asset builds, with per-app pins via `cipi app edit --node-version=`; servers still on end-of-life Node 20 move to 22; a hash-chained, root-only deploy audit ledger (/var/log/cipi/deploys.jsonl, mirrored to syslog) that records every deploy however it started, read with `cipi deploy <app> --audit` and verified by `cipi compliance deploys`; cipi.yml gains app.www, app.basic_auth, redirect, redirects, proxies, node, search, deploy recipe options, app.limits, ssl.force_https, env.required and crons; fixed: pre-5.1 and removed-profile backups were never pruned and S3 retention errors were swallowed, and `cipi api update` notified every night. 5.3.1: read-only `cipi compliance` evidence for ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and SOC 2 audits — 17 controls, checksummed root-only report bundle, no secrets exported, known gaps such as the vault's AES-256-CBC without MAC stated in the report; `cipi redirect` for app-wide and path redirects and `cipi proxy` for reverse proxy prefixes, both stored in apps.json and restored if `nginx -t` fails; CLI only, no migration. 5.3.0: opt-in Cloudflare Zero Trust via `cipi zt` — API token root-only in /etc/cipi/zt.token (separate from the certbot DNS-01 file), `enable` installs cloudflared with a locally-managed tunnel and writes nginx real_ip (CF-Connecting-IP) plus fail2ban/CrowdSec allowlists of Cloudflare's ranges without closing 22/80/443; `hostname add` routes an app or the GUI through the tunnel (public CDN/WAF), `access enable` puts Cloudflare Access in front (with a /cipi/webhook bypass for Git webhooks), `ssh enable` carries SSH over the tunnel; `lock http` refuses while an app renews Let's Encrypt over HTTP-01 and then closes 80/443 or limits them to Cloudflare IPs, `lock ssh` refuses unless cloudflared is healthy with SSH ingress (rescue `cipi zt ssh unlock`); optional 15-year Origin CA via `cipi zt origin-cert`; `disable` restores UFW. `cipi monitor` — server checks every 5 minutes from cron (disk ≥80/90%, SSL expiry ≤14 days, services, queue workers/Horizon, 5xx ≥20 and ≥5%, read-only /etc/cipi or /var/log/cipi, load >4× cores for 2 runs), edge-triggered alerts with recovery and a 4-hour reminder, `monitor_*` triggers, on by default. Alert channels — `cipi notifications channel add slack|discord|telegram|ntfy|webhook` fans every notification out to chat, no SMTP required, 5-second timeout, failures only logged. Fixed: jq `// true` read false as true, so muted triggers kept firing, `cipi smtp configure --tls=off` was ignored and `health: {enabled: false}` in cipi.yml did nothing. 5.2.3: `cipi git` auto-setup beyond GitHub/GitLab — Cursor Origin, AWS CodeCommit, Bitbucket Cloud and Azure DevOps detected from the SSH clone URL, deploy key always registered, webhook where the forge has one (Bitbucket repo:push + HMAC secret, Azure git.push service hook sending X-Gitlab-Token; Origin and CodeCommit have none); `deploy.post` in cipi.yml — allowlisted post-deploy steps (artisan, npm/npx/yarn/pnpm, composer, one relative php/node script), no free shell, and the one section that runs without `cipi yml auto`, with `post_on_failure: warn|abort` and `cipi yml post-deploy <app>`; manual patch-level stack upgrades for the packages kept off unattended-upgrades — `cipi nginx upgrade`, `cipi db upgrade [mariadb|pgsql]`, `cipi service upgrade [nginx|mariadb|postgresql|valkey]`, never on a cron and `all` refused; security fix: a custom app's committed cipi.yml was downloadable at https://domain/cipi.yml — every app vhost now denies /cipi.yml and /cipi.yaml at any path. 5.2.2: opt-in Meilisearch for Laravel Scout via `cipi search` and an allowlisted `cipi package` for host binaries; 5.2.0: opt-in CrowdSec — engine plus a registered firewall bouncer, a rescue TLS listener with a one-shot break-glass token, and no WAF — plus a nightly 04:40 integrity scan of the live release against the sha256 manifest written at each deploy, ClamAV on upload dirs only, and bash/zsh tab-completion installed automatically; nothing is enabled by setup.sh or self-update. 5.1.3 hotfix: `cipi ini list` no longer dies on the first setting after printing the header; 5.1.2 Reverb production-ready: generated credentials, ws/wss from the certificate, proxy limited to /app/{key} and /apps/{id}/…, raised connection limits, workers.reverb in cipi.yml; 5.1.1 hotfix: FPM pool repair and wildcard domains end to end; 5.1.0: backup profiles, cipi.yml, cipi ini, post-deploy healthchecks, nginx default-server, wildcard aliases; plus Laravel Octane on FrankenPHP, Horizon, PostgreSQL, Node build on deploy, pre-deploy snapshots, wildcard SSL via DNS-01, staging clones)

## Core capabilities

- One-command install of the full LEMP production stack on any Ubuntu VPS
- Isolated apps: each app gets its own system user, PHP-FPM pool (or Octane service), Nginx vhost and database
- Zero-downtime Git deployments via webhooks from GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket Cloud or Azure DevOps (deploy keys and webhooks configured automatically; Cursor Origin and AWS CodeCommit get the deploy key only), Deployer-style releases
- Laravel Octane on FrankenPHP: `cipi app create --octane`, `cipi app convert --to=octane`; Octane apps run beside classic FPM apps
- Laravel Horizon, Reverb, queue workers (Supervisor) and scheduler configured out of the box
- Databases: MariaDB default, optional PostgreSQL (`cipi db install pgsql`), per-app engine choice (`--engine=mariadb|pgsql`)
- SSL: free Let's Encrypt certificates (`cipi ssl install`), wildcard via DNS-01 with the Cloudflare API (`cipi alias add <app> '*.example.com'` + `cipi ssl install <app> --dns=cloudflare`; several named Cloudflare accounts since 5.5.0; installed by Cipi itself since 5.5.1), forced HTTPS (`cipi ssl force`). Behind the Cloudflare proxy use SSL/TLS Full (strict), never Flexible. Guide with and without Cloudflare: https://cipi.sh/docs/advanced#wildcard-domains
- www redirects: `cipi www add|force-to-root|force-from-root|clear|status` — since 5.7.2 also for a wildcard primary (`*.example.com`): the pair is example.com ↔ www.example.com
- Default app (5.7.2+): `cipi use <app>` makes the per-app commands (`cipi deploy`, `cipi app logs|env|artisan`, `cipi yml plan|apply`, `cipi worker list`, `cipi ssl install`, `cipi www`, `cipi alias`, …) act on it when no app is given; `cipi use` shows it, `cipi use --clear` removes it, `CIPI_APP=<app>` does the same for one shell; commands where a missing app means every app, and destructive ones, are untouched
- Environments (5.8.0+): `cipi app create … --env=<label>` (optional, default `production`; lowercase letters, digits, `-`, `_`, max 32 chars), `cipi app edit <app> --env=<label>`, `cipi app clone <src> --env=<label>` (default: the source app's env), `cipi app show` prints "Environment"; Cipi writes `APP_ENV=<label>` (Laravel) and `CIPI_ENV=<label>` (Laravel and Node) into `shared/.env` next to `CIPI_DEPLOY_BRANCH`, `cipi sync import|update` keep them in step, migration 5.8.0 adds `CIPI_ENV=production` to apps that lack it (an existing value is left alone); apps without the key are `production`. Per-environment cipi.yml: an app with env `<label>` reads `cipi-<label>.yml` (or `.yaml`) first and falls back to `cipi.yml`/`cipi.yaml` in each place it already looked (`current/`, a custom app's `htdocs/`, then `shared/`) — a production app reads `cipi-production.yml` then `cipi.yml`; one repository serves staging (`cipi-staging.yml`) and production (`cipi.yml` or `cipi-production.yml`); the file is chosen by the server (the app's env), never by the file; an invalid `cipi-<label>.yml` has no fallback and the error names the file; `cipi yml auto <app> status` prints the environment and the file in use, `cipi yml plan <app> --json` and `cipi yml auto <app> --json` include `env`, `cipi yml generate <app>` names the file to commit (`cipi-<env>.yml` when the env is not production); nginx denies `/cipi-<anything>.yml|yaml` (migration 5.8.0 updates vhosts). cipi.yml `deploy.branch` (string): the git branch the app deploys, validated like `cipi app edit --branch` (`^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._/-]{0,190}$`, no `..`); `cipi yml plan` shows `deploy branch: main → develop (from the next deploy)`, `cipi yml apply` sets it like `cipi app edit --branch` (apps.json, deploy.php, the webhook's `CIPI_DEPLOY_BRANCH`), blocked when the app has no repository, applies from the next deploy — typical: `cipi-staging.yml` with `deploy: { branch: develop }` and `cipi.yml` with `deploy: { branch: main }`; `cipi yml generate` emits it. Ecosystem: the REST API (cipi/api 1.36.0, MCP server 1.6.0) accepts `env` on app create/update and returns it on app objects and `GET /api/apps/{name}/yml`; cipi-cli 1.9.0 `app create --env`, `app edit --env`, `app show`; PHP SDK 1.4.0 `Apps::create(['env' => …])`; GUI 4.0.0: the create/edit app forms have an Environment field and the cipi.yml tab shows the env; cipi/agent 2.1.0 carries the env in `cipi:status`, `app_info`, `deploy_status`, the webhook answer and the health report, its cipi.yml locator reads `cipi-<env>.yml` first and its validator knows `deploy.branch`; Cipi Studio 2.4.17: env badge, env field on new/edit app in the connector, a downloadable starter named `cipi-<env>.yml`
- Backups: profile-driven (`cipi backup profile`) — S3-compatible / local, client-side encryption, verify, overdue watchdog; pre-deploy database snapshots; `cipi db restore`; `cipi backup profile remove <name> --purge` (5.7.2+) also deletes every archive the profile wrote, on every destination
- Security: AES-256-CBC config encryption at rest, hardened defaults, PHP security patches managed by Cipi (`cipi php upgrade`, daily at 03:30 since 5.6.3; it reports the patch level of each PHP version and Octane FrankenPHP binary, and FPM pools carry the 2026-10-21 advisory hardening flags — since 5.7.2 also in each version's fpm/conf.d/99-cipi.ini and with file_uploads off in the Node webhook pool); nginx, MariaDB, PostgreSQL and Valkey patched on demand with `cipi nginx upgrade` / `cipi db upgrade` / `cipi service upgrade` (v5.2.3+)
- IP reputation (v5.2.0+, opt-in): `cipi crowdsec enable` installs the CrowdSec engine and a registered firewall bouncer, reads the per-vhost Nginx logs, allowlists your SSH session, GitHub webhook CIDRs and Let's Encrypt, and starts a rescue TLS listener so an automatic ban cannot lock you out; `cipi ban list|unban` covers both CrowdSec and fail2ban. Not a WAF
- Integrity + malware scan (v5.2.0+, opt-in): `cipi scan` verifies nightly that the live release still matches the sha256 manifest written at its deploy (manifests kept root-only in /var/lib/cipi/manifests), then runs ClamAV over the upload directories only; alerts are `scan_integrity` or `scan_incomplete`
- Shell tab-completion (v5.2.0+): bash and zsh completion for verbs, sub-commands, flags and app names, installed by `setup.sh` and every `cipi self-update`; works after `sudo cipi` and in `sudo -s`/`su`/tmux shells since 5.5.0
- Search (v5.2.2+, opt-in): `cipi search` installs Meilisearch as a native binary on 127.0.0.1 for Laravel Scout; Cipi writes SCOUT_PREFIX; not in cipi backup
- Git forges (v5.2.3+): GitHub, GitLab, Cursor Origin, AWS CodeCommit, Bitbucket Cloud, Azure DevOps — `cipi git <provider>-token`, `remove-<provider>`, `cipi git refresh` covers them all; since 5.6.0 the deploy key is tested against the repository on `cipi app create`, `cipi app edit --repository=`/`--branch=` and `cipi git check [app]` (`git ls-remote` as the app user), and on a terminal a refused read offers to save or replace the forge token, then registers key and webhook; since 5.7.2 a refused deploy key or webhook says what the forge answered and what the token needs (a GitHub 404 is a token that cannot see the repository), `cipi git refresh` no longer rotates the key on a 404, and the app's deploy branch is written to .env as `CIPI_DEPLOY_BRANCH` so a push to another branch is skipped
- Manual stack upgrades (v5.2.3+): `cipi nginx upgrade`, `cipi db upgrade [engine]`, `cipi service upgrade [name]` — patch-level, operator-triggered, mails nginx_upgrade/mariadb_upgrade/pgsql_upgrade/valkey_upgrade
- Cloudflare Zero Trust (v5.3.0+, opt-in): `cipi zt enable` (tunnel + nginx real_ip, ports stay open), `cipi zt hostname add <app|--gui>`, `cipi zt access enable <app|--gui>`, `cipi zt ssh enable --hostname=`, `cipi zt lock http|ssh` with refusals that prevent lock-outs, `cipi zt origin-cert <app>`; fail2ban and UFW stay
- System monitor (v5.3.0+): `cipi monitor` checks disk, per-app disk limits (`app_disk`, 5.5.0+), SSL expiry, services, workers, 5xx spikes, read-only filesystems and load every 5 minutes; `cipi monitor list|enable|disable|set|test`; alerts on state change and recovery only
- Alert channels (v5.3.0+): `cipi notifications channel add <slack|discord|telegram|ntfy|webhook> <id>` — every notification trigger also reaches chat; best-effort, never blocks a deploy
- Compliance evidence (v5.3.1+, read-only): `cipi compliance [check] [--days=90] [--json]` — 17 controls mapped to ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A and SOC 2 TSC, exits 1 on any fail; `cipi compliance report` writes report.md, report.json, evidence/ and SHA256SUMS plus a .tar.gz and .sha256 under /var/log/cipi/compliance; `list`, `controls`
- Node apps (v5.4.0+): `cipi app create --node=spa|static|ssr [--framework=next|nuxt|sveltekit|astro|remix|vite] [--node-version=22|24] [--build=] [--start=] [--output=] [--health-path=]`; SSR blue/green deploys with a health gate; `cipi node status|restart|logs <app>`; `cipi node install|list|upgrade|remove|default` for runtimes
- Disk usage and soft limits (v5.5.0+): `cipi disk [--json]`, `cipi disk db [--json]`; `cipi app limits <app> --disk=<GB>|none` (default none, alerts only via the `app_disk` monitor check, trigger `monitor_app_disk`). Since Cipi 5.5.2 / API 1.33: `GET /api/disk`, `GET /api/disk/dbs` (`disk-view`); the soft limit is `GET|PUT /api/apps/{name}/limits` since API 1.32
- cipi.yml from the panel (Cipi 5.6.4+ / API 1.35): `cipi yml plan <app> --json`, `cipi yml auto <app> status --json` (both with `env` since Cipi 5.8.0 / API 1.36.0, `file` being the `cipi-<env>.yml` in use); `GET /api/apps/{name}/yml` (`yml-view`), `POST /api/apps/{name}/yml/apply` (job `app-yml-apply`) and `POST /api/apps/{name}/yml/auto/enable|disable` (`yml-manage`); MCP `AppYmlShow`, `AppYmlApply`, `AppYmlAuto`; a cipi.yml tab in the GUI, `cipi-cli yml`, `$cipi->yml()` in the PHP SDK. Auto-apply covers `cipi deploy`, panel/API deploys and the Git webhook (the webhook path works since 5.6.4)
- SSH access and brute-force threshold (v5.5.0+): `cipi ssh apps [--json]`, `cipi ssh apps enable|disable <app>|--all`; `cipi firewall attempts [<1-100>|default]`
- Deploy status (v5.8.4+): `cipi deploy <app> --status [--json] [--tail=N]` reads the start/end banners both deploy paths write to `/home/<app>/logs/deploy.log` plus the live processes (Deployer, the webhook wrapper cipi-app-deploy, `cipi deploy`): `state` running (`phase` deploy while Deployer builds, post-deploy while post steps/cipi.yml/healthcheck run), queued (`~/.deploy-trigger` waiting for the per-minute cron), interrupted (start banner without end and nothing alive — reboot/kill; the lock is what `--unlock` removes), idle; `current` {trigger, branch, from_release, started_at (ISO 8601 with offset), elapsed, pids}, `last` {result ok/failed, kind deploy/rollback, release, duration, exit, trigger, branch, started_at, finished_at}, `locked`, `queued`, `tail` with --tail; the start banner of a panel-run `cipi deploy` says trigger=panel; panel API `GET /api/apps/{name}/deploy/status[?tail=N]` (cipi/api 1.37.0, `deploy-manage`, 503 on Cipi < 5.8.4) polled by cipi/gui 4.1.0
- Deploy audit ledger (v5.4.0+): every deploy (CLI, panel, webhook, SSH, cron, in-app MCP) recorded root-side with verified origin, operator, IP and commit, app claims kept apart, hash-chained and mirrored to syslog; `cipi deploy <app> --audit [--days=90] [--json]`
- Redirects and proxy prefixes (v5.3.1+, panel API and GUI since 5.4.1): `cipi redirect set|enable|disable|unset` (whole app, one hop, path kept unless --no-path), `cipi redirect add|remove|list` (exact or prefix paths), `cipi proxy add|remove|list <app> <prefix> <upstream> [--strip-prefix] [--preserve-host] [--timeout=] [--no-buffering]`; triggers redirect_change, proxy_change
- Host packages (v5.2.2+, opt-in): `cipi package list|install|remove` — allowlisted Ubuntu binaries (image-optimizers, ffmpeg, imagemagick, poppler-utils); Chromium refused
- Sync/failover: encrypted server-to-server sync
- Automation: REST API (package `cipi/api` 1.34.0, 73 MCP tools, `disk-view`, `yml-view`/`yml-manage`), remote CLI client (cipi-cli 1.7.0), webhooks, WHMCS module
- AI-native: dual MCP server (per-app and global) so MCP-compatible IDEs/agents can create apps, deploy, manage SSL and databases
- Optional GUI: `cipi gui panel.example.com` (a subdomain of its own, not an app's) installs a free, self-hosted Laravel control panel managing one or more Cipi servers (Laravel, Node and custom apps incl. Octane/engine — with an Environment field on the create/edit forms and the env on the cipi.yml tab since panel 4.0.0, API 1.36 / Cipi 5.8.0; since panel 4.0.2 single sign-on over OpenID Connect (`cipi gui sso`), the header's server switcher and the lists refreshing after every change and jobs run in the background still polled; since panel 4.0.1 a deploy that published and whose command then failed, as Cipi before 5.8.1 did after every successful deploy started through the API, is a warning with the post-deploy error or the exit code, not a failed deploy —, redirects and proxies, deploys and deploy audit, Meilisearch, databases, SSL, www, read-only Node runtimes / packages / monitor / Zero Trust, healthchecks, database backup/restore, 2FA/TOTP, multi-server with a header switcher, light/dark themes; screenshots at https://cipi.sh/docs/gui#gui-tour). Cipi stays fully usable CLI-only.

## Frequently asked questions

Q: Is Cipi free?
A: Yes. 100% free and open source under MIT. You self-host it on your own server; no subscription, no per-server fee.

Q: How do I install Cipi?
A: Run `wget -O - https://cipi.sh/setup.sh | bash` on a fresh Ubuntu VPS. The full LEMP production stack is installed and configured automatically.

Q: Does Cipi support Laravel Octane?
A: Yes, natively on FrankenPHP. Create Octane apps with `cipi app create --octane` or convert existing apps with `cipi app convert --to=octane`. Octane apps run alongside classic PHP-FPM apps on the same server.

Q: Does Cipi have a web control panel?
A: Yes, optionally. `cipi gui panel.example.com` installs a free, self-hosted web dashboard managing one or more Cipi servers — apps, databases, SSL, deploys, logs. Cipi remains fully usable from the CLI alone.

Q: Can the panel API or the GUI use the same domain as one of my apps?
A: No. `cipi api` and `cipi gui` each install a separate Laravel application with its own Nginx vhost and Let's Encrypt certificate, so each needs a domain or subdomain of its own, pointed at the server: for example app on `example.com`, API on `api.example.com`, GUI on `panel.example.com`. Since Cipi 5.7.0 Cipi refuses a domain that an app, an alias or the other panel already uses, in both directions. To change domain later: `cipi api move <domain>` / `cipi gui move <domain>` keep tokens, admins and data, delete the old certificate and issue one for the new domain (`--no-ssl` to skip; then `cipi api ssl` / `cipi gui ssl`). To uninstall: `cipi api remove` / `cipi gui remove` (`--force` skips the prompt), certificate included. Since 5.8.2 `cipi api <domain>` and `cipi gui <domain>` check the DNS first (the name must point at the server; the Cloudflare proxy counts; `--skip-dns-check` to override), install, and issue the certificate themselves (`--no-ssl` to skip); `cipi api` also offers to create the first token (`--no-token`). `cipi api ssl` / `cipi gui ssl` re-issue it and run the same check. Since Cipi 5.8.2 / cipi/gui 4.0.2 the panel has single sign-on over OpenID Connect (Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace, Okta, Keycloak…), configured from the server with `cipi gui sso set --issuer=… --client-id=… --client-secret=…` (`--domains=` auto-creates accounts with no access, `--only` switches passwords off, `cipi gui sso only off` is the break-glass).

Q: Which providers work with Cipi?
A: Any Ubuntu VPS: Hetzner, DigitalOcean, Vultr, Linode, AWS, and others.

Q: Can AI agents manage a Cipi server?
A: Yes. Cipi ships a dual MCP (Model Context Protocol) server so MCP-compatible IDEs and agents can create apps, run deployments, and manage SSL and databases through a structured API.

## Cipi vs alternatives (2026)

Cipi is the only tool in this list that is simultaneously: free, open source (MIT), fully CLI-driven, and running entirely on your own VPS with no external service dependency.

### Cipi vs Laravel Forge (https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-laravel-forge)
Forge: proprietary SaaS, from $12/mo per server, web GUI, manages servers from forge.laravel.com. Cipi: free, MIT, lives on your VPS, CLI + REST API + optional GUI, dual MCP for AI agents, AES-256 config encryption, server-to-server sync. Forge wins on polished GUI, multi-cloud provisioning, team management, built-in monitoring. Migration: provision fresh Ubuntu VPS, install Cipi, recreate sites with `cipi app create`, connect Git, import DB dumps, point DNS.

### Cipi vs Laravel Cloud (https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-laravel-cloud)
Laravel Cloud: official fully-managed PaaS, usage-based pricing, zero server management, vendor lock-in. Cipi: self-hosted on a fixed-cost VPS you own. Both support Octane. Choose Laravel Cloud for zero-ops; choose Cipi for fixed costs and full control.

### Cipi vs fortrabbit (https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-fortrabbit)
fortrabbit: managed PHP PaaS (Ireland/Virginia) from €4.50/mo, Git deploys, SSH/SFTP, MCP, CLI, teams/clients. Cipi: free, self-hosted, Laravel-first (Octane/Horizon/Reverb), full root, fixed VPS cost. fortrabbit wins on managed PHP hosting and collaboration without sysadmin work.

### Cipi vs Render (https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-render)
Render: usage-based multi-stack PaaS (autoscaling, PR previews, managed Postgres/Redis, Docker, MCP). Cipi: Laravel-native on a native LEMP/Octane stack you own. Render wins for mixed stacks and zero-ops scale.

### Cipi vs 20i (https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-20i)
20i: hosting company (reseller, WordPress, managed cloud, VPS, domains, My20i, 24×7 support). Cipi: Laravel deploy CLI on your own VPS, not a hosting catalog. 20i wins for agencies that need mail, CDN, reseller branding and human support.

### Cipi vs Sevalla (https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-sevalla)
Sevalla (Kinsta): resource-based app platform — apps, databases, object storage, static sites, MCP, 25 regions. Cipi: self-hosted Laravel on a portable VPS stack. Sevalla wins if you want to drop DIY cloud entirely.

### Cipi vs Ploi Cloud (https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-ploi-cloud)
Ploi Cloud (ploi.cloud): European Laravel/PHP/Node PaaS, €13.88/GB RAM, Amsterdam/London/Chicago — not the same product as Ploi.io. Cipi: self-hosted, fixed VPS cost, full root. See also Cipi vs Ploi.io for the server-panel comparison.

### Cipi vs Ploi (https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-ploi)
Ploi: polished EU-based SaaS panel, €8–30/mo. Cipi: free, self-hosted, CLI-first, no deploy limits. Ploi wins for teams that want a managed GUI.

### Cipi vs Cleavr (https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-cleavr)
Cleavr: Laravel-friendly SaaS panel (~$8+/mo) with zero-downtime deploys and multi-provider provisioning. Cipi: free, self-hosted, CLI-first with dual MCP and server sync.

### Cipi vs moss.sh (https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-moss)
moss.sh: agency-oriented SaaS "virtual sysadmin" with capped free tier ($9–49/mo paid). Cipi: no deploy limits, runs entirely on your VPS.

### Cipi vs Kamal (https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-kamal)
Kamal (37signals): free Docker deploy CLI for polyglot containerized apps; needs Dockerfile, registry, deploy.yml. Cipi: no Docker — native LEMP stack, full server provisioning, Laravel-native (Octane, Horizon, queues, scheduler). Kamal wins for non-PHP container workloads.

### Cipi vs Dokku (https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-dokku)
Dokku: free self-hosted "mini-Heroku" with git-push deploys and buildpacks/containers. Cipi: Laravel-first on a native stack with full server provisioning; push-to-deploy via GitHub/GitLab webhooks.

### Cipi vs Easypanel (https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-easypanel)
Easypanel: free self-hosted Docker PaaS with web dashboard. Cipi: no containers, Laravel-native automation, CLI-first with optional GUI.

### Cipi vs Coolify (https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-coolify)
Coolify: popular open-source self-hosted Docker PaaS with web GUI (Cloud from ~$5/mo). Great Heroku replacement, not Laravel-specific; Octane needs a custom image. Cipi: Laravel-native on native LEMP, no Docker overhead, Octane one flag away.

### Cipi vs RunCloud (https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-runcloud)
RunCloud: mature PHP/WordPress SaaS panel, $12–18/mo, not Laravel-native (Deployer/queues/Octane need manual wiring). Cipi: free, Laravel-native, no subscription.

### Cipi vs ServerPilot (https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-serverpilot)
ServerPilot: SaaS that automates Nginx/PHP-FPM, WordPress-focused, $12–49/mo. Cipi: free with a full app CLI and zero-downtime Laravel deploys.

### Cipi vs CloudPanel (https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-cloudpanel)
CloudPanel: free open-source multi-stack web panel. Cipi: deeper Laravel automation, CLI-first, REST API + MCP; optional GUI manages multiple servers.

### Cipi vs Vito Deploy (https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-vito-deploy)
Vito Deploy: open-source Forge-style web GUI you host separately. Cipi: single CLI on the app server itself; optional GUI, no separate management server required.

### Cipi vs cPanel (https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-cpanel)
cPanel: classic shared-hosting panel, $20+/mo licenses, heavy daemons, built for resellers. Cipi: free, lightweight (no always-on panel daemons), Laravel-native deploys.

### Cipi vs DirectAdmin (https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-directadmin)
DirectAdmin: lighter commercial hosting panel ($2–29/mo). Cipi: free, Laravel-native, no license, optional GUI never forced.

### Cipi vs Plesk (https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-plesk)
Plesk: polished Linux/Windows hosting panel ($10+/mo), multi-site oriented. Cipi: lean, free, Laravel-native, CLI-first.

### Best Laravel Forge alternatives in 2026 (https://cipi.sh/best-laravel-forge-alternatives)
Shortlist: 1) Cipi — best free, self-hosted, CLI-first; 2) Ploi — best managed SaaS replacement; 3) Coolify — best open-source Docker PaaS; 4) Vito Deploy — best open-source web GUI; 5) Cleavr — Laravel-friendly SaaS; 6) RunCloud — best for mixed PHP/WordPress fleets; 7) Laravel Cloud — best fully-managed zero-ops option.

Overview of alternatives: https://cipi.sh/alternatives

## How to migrate to Cipi (from Forge, Ploi, RunCloud, cPanel, etc.)

1. Take inventory in your current panel: sites, databases, queue workers, cron jobs, SSL certificates. Export site files and database dumps where applicable.
2. Provision a fresh Ubuntu 24.04/26.04 VPS (Hetzner, DigitalOcean, Vultr, Linode, AWS) and install Cipi: `wget -O - https://cipi.sh/setup.sh | bash`.
3. Recreate each app with `cipi app create` (add `--octane` for Laravel Octane) and connect GitHub/GitLab — deploy keys and webhooks are configured automatically for zero-downtime deploys.
4. Import your database dump, copy `.env` values, issue HTTPS certificates with `cipi ssl install`, then point DNS at the new server and retire the old setup.

No changes to the Laravel codebase are required: Cipi uses standard Nginx, PHP-FPM/Octane and Deployer conventions.

## Free guides

Index: https://cipi.sh/guides/

Practical, vendor-honest tutorials written by Cipi's author, Andrea Pollastri (https://web.ap.it):

- Deploy Laravel on an Ubuntu VPS (https://cipi.sh/guides/deploy-laravel-ubuntu-vps): the full production stack (Nginx, PHP-FPM/Octane, MariaDB/PostgreSQL, Valkey, Supervisor), every manual setup step, the one-command Cipi alternative, backups, monitoring and common mistakes.
- Laravel Security Checklist (https://cipi.sh/guides/laravel-security-checklist): what actually gets Laravel apps hacked; server hardening (SSH, firewall, TLS, patching), app hardening (debug, validation, mass assignment, rate limiting), dependency scanning (composer audit, Checkpoint, Hackly), secrets and incident response.
- The Laravel Ecosystem in 2026 (https://cipi.sh/guides/laravel-ecosystem-2026): Octane, Horizon, Reverb, Livewire vs Inertia, Filament, Pest/Larastan/Pint, observability, and the hosting spectrum from Laravel Cloud to self-hosted Cipi.
- CI/CD for Laravel (https://cipi.sh/guides/laravel-ci-cd-git-workflow): trunk-based Git workflow, a complete GitHub Actions pipeline (Pint, Larastan, Pest, composer audit), zero-downtime deploy options (webhook push-to-deploy, CI-driven, hybrid) and expand/contract migrations.
- Spec-Driven Development with AI Agents (https://cipi.sh/guides/spec-driven-development-ai-laravel): specs as repo artifacts, MCP (Model Context Protocol), guardrails for agent-written code, and a spec-to-production loop using Cipi's MCP/API for safe agent deploys.
- The Self-Hosted Laravel Developer Stack (https://cipi.sh/guides/laravel-developer-stack-2026): a full stack you own — Cipi (deploys), Boogle (exception tracking), Indiestats (analytics), Johnny (S3-compatible storage), Newsletter, Checkpoint + Hackly (security), Init, Conn, Mister Dev, 127001.it — for roughly the price of one VPS.
- Several buckets (v5.6.0+): `cipi backup destination add <name> --bucket= --key= --secret= [--region=] [--endpoint=]`, `list|show|test|edit|remove`; profiles take `--dest=local,s3,<name>`, `cipi.yml` `destinations: [s3, <name>]`; the bucket of `cipi backup configure` stays the default `s3`
- Back Up a VPS to an S3 Bucket (https://cipi.sh/guides/backup-vps-s3): why same-disk dumps are not backups; what Cipi uploads (`db.sql.gz` + `shared.tar.gz`); `cipi backup configure` for AWS/Hetzner/Spaces/B2/MinIO/Johnny; cron + prune; restore drill onto a new VPS.
- Deploy WordPress on Cipi (https://cipi.sh/guides/deploy-wordpress-custom-app): host WordPress as a Cipi custom app (`cipi app create --custom`) with MariaDB (`cipi db create`), SSL and a GitHub Actions pipeline that SSHs in and runs `sudo cipi deploy`. Keep wp-config.php and wp-content/uploads out of Git. The Laravel Agent webhook is not used.
- Use cipi/agent in Laravel (https://cipi.sh/guides/cipi-agent-laravel-mcp): install `composer require cipi/agent`, enable the in-app MCP (`php artisan cipi:service mcp --enable`), connect Cursor/VS Code/Claude Code/Claude Desktop to `POST /cipi/mcp`. Eleven tools: health, app_info, deploy, deploy_status, logs, artisan, db_query, db_schema, env_check, cipi_yml, anonymizer (plus panel_status, panel_deploy_audit, panel_rollback, panel_db_backup, panel_job via cipi/sdk). Use named seeders on staging (`db:seed --class=RoleSeeder`); `migrate:fresh`, `migrate:reset` and `db:wipe` are blocked since 2.0. Distinct from the panel API MCP (73 server tools).
- Cipi Control Panel and API (https://cipi.sh/guides/cipi-gui-and-api): optional `cipi/api` (REST + 73 MCP tools + Swagger, 1.34.0) and `cipi/gui` (Laravel 12/13 + Livewire multi-server dashboard, v3.1, Server → Disk). Same API powers cipi-cli, the PHP SDK (`cipi/sdk`), and WHMCS. CLI-first: both packages are opt-in; remove them and Cipi is a CLI again.

## Pricing summary

- Cipi: $0 forever, MIT license. You pay only for your VPS (from ~$5–7/mo at Hetzner/DigitalOcean/Vultr). One VPS can host multiple Laravel apps.
- Laravel Forge: from $12/mo per server. Laravel Cloud: usage-based. Ploi: €8–30/mo. Cleavr: ~$8+/mo. RunCloud: $12–18/mo. ServerPilot: $12–49/mo. cPanel: $20+/mo. Plesk: $10+/mo. DirectAdmin: $2–29/mo. Coolify/Vito/Kamal/Dokku/CloudPanel: free (self-hosted).

the trigger file carries source/actor/ip/ref/request_id, recorded as claims in the deploy audit ledger); health `GET /cipi/health` (app debug/maintenance, database, cache, queue pending + failed jobs, storage and disk, deploy release/commit from Deployer REVISION, in_progress, pending, last_deploy; degraded only when database/cache/queue/storage fail); in-app MCP `POST /cipi/mcp` (Bearer `CIPI_MCP_TOKEN`, off by default; Streamable HTTP; revisions 2024-11-05, 2025-03-26, 2025-06-18, 2025-11-25 via initialize and 2026-07-28 via server/discover with _meta, resultType and Mcp-Method/Mcp-Name validation; tools carry title, annotations, structuredContent, isError; GET/DELETE 405; Origin checked against the app host, `CIPI_MCP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`) with 11 tools — health, app_info, deploy (actor/ref/request_id), deploy_status, logs (laravel|nginx|php|worker|horizon|reverb|deploy|all, level, search; `php artisan cipi:yml validate [--json] [--strict] | show | generate [--write] | example [--write] | schema [--write]` ports the server's cipi.yml validator with identical messages, checks env.required against the local .env and infers a first file from the app (Horizon/queues, Reverb, Scout, scheduler, /up, PHP version, namespaced databases, .env.example credentials); anonymizer for MySQL/MariaDB and PostgreSQL (pg_dump plain, COPY blocks and INSERTs) — `POST /cipi/db` {email, gzip}, `POST /cipi/db/user`, signed `GET /cipi/db/{token}` valid `CIPI_ANONYMIZER_TTL` minutes; config `/home/<app>/.db/anonymization.json` with transformations (name, `type:arg` or object with unique/consistent), truncate and options (hash_algorithm, password, faker_locale, consistent, seed, gzip, connection, dump_args); 47 transformations incl. password (hash of options.password, computed once), null, fixed, hash, mask, redact, keep; `cipi:init-anonymize --scan` proposes the config from the schema, `cipi:anonymize-audit` checks it, `cipi:anonymize [--gzip] [--check] [--transformations]` runs it on the server; `cipi-cli db anonymize` drives the anonymizer from the terminal through the Cipi API — it reads APP_URL and CIPI_ANONYMIZER_TOKEN from the app .env, POSTs /cipi/db, the agent emails a signed link that `cipi-cli db anonymize download` saves): https://cipi.sh/docs/agent
